title: AAA — pulsatile abdominal mass + back pain (USMLE CVS case)

properties.cases overview: 75M with lower back pain; hx smoking (45 pack-years), HTN, hyperlipidemia; obese, limited back ROM; palpable pulsatile mass left/superior to umbilicus → concern for AAA. Discussion focused on differentiating aneurysm (dilation) vs thrombotic occlusion; ultrasound for screening/confirmation; CTA for pre-op planning.
properties.feedback:
Key feedback points from our discussion:
- Problem representation improved after explicitly including “pulsatile abdominal mass near umbilicus”.
- Corrected misconception: pulse deficit (HR≠PR) is more typical of AF; dissection clues are pulse asymmetry/BP difference, tearing pain, new AR murmur.
- Corrected mechanism: AAA is vessel wall weakening (esp. media support/elastin) → dilation, not lumen occlusion; occlusion presents with distal ischemia.
- Imaging reasoning: US for screening/initial measurement in stable patient; CTA for anatomical detail and operative/EVAR planning.
- Anatomy reinforcement: aortic hiatus at T12; abdominal aorta runs slightly left of midline; branches/infrarenal location commonly involved.
